decision_reason: Iteration 1 successfully identified the primary CDC NoroSTAT surveillance pages, several high-quality news/clinical media sources with quantified outbreak counts for December 2024 and January 2025, and one state-level source (Minnesota). However, critical gaps remain: (1) No data covering January–February 2025 weekly outbreak counts beyond the week ending Jan. 9 has been surfaced in snippets; (2) The CDC NORS dashboard for structured outbreak-level records (with subnational location, setting, hospitalizations, deaths) was not directly returned as a result; (3) Only one state health department source (Minnesota) appeared — subnational/locality coverage is thin; (4) CDC cruise ship outbreak data for December 2024 was mentioned in a CIDRAP snippet but not directly sourced; (5) Deaths and hospitalizations fields remain unaddressed by any snippet; (6) The February 2025 portion of the time window has no coverage yet. A second iteration targeting: (a) the CDC NORS dashboard directly, (b) February 2025 norovirus data, (c) additional state-level outbreak reports, and (d) CDC cruise ship/vessel outbreak data will materially improve coverage of the target fields.
coverage_assessment: Partial. The Dec 2024 – early Jan 2025 window has good national-level outbreak count coverage via NoroSTAT snippets (495 outbreaks Aug–Dec 11 2024; 91 outbreaks week of Dec 5; 128 outbreaks week prior to Jan 9; 97 outbreaks week ending Jan 9). The Feb 2025 window is entirely uncovered. Subnational/locality coverage is limited to one Minnesota state health department result. Deaths and hospitalizations are not yet evidenced in any snippet. The NORS structured database — the primary source for outbreak-level records with setting, cases, hospitalizations, deaths — was not returned as a direct result despite being queried.
source_diversity_assessment: Moderate. Sources span CDC official pages (5 results), clinical/medical media (contemporarypediatrics.com, mdedge.com, infectiousdiseaseadvisor.com, contagionlive.com), general news (today.com, cbsnews.com, nbcnews.com), academic (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), and one state health department (health.state.mn.us). Social media (facebook.com, instagram.com, youtube.com) and non-authoritative mirrors (restoredcdc.org) are present but low-value. Missing: direct NORS database results, additional state health department pages, CDC vessel/cruise ship outbreak page, and any WHO/PAHO or ProMED international situation report referencing US norovirus.
trustworthiness_assessment: High for CDC-origin results. The cdc.gov NoroSTAT data page and data table are authoritative. Clinical media (contemporarypediatrics.com, mdedge.com, infectiousdiseaseadvisor.com) cite CDC figures directly and are acceptable collection-support sources. CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a highly trusted academic public health news outlet. The Minnesota state health department result is authoritative for subnational data. restoredcdc.org is a mirror/archive site — lower trust, should be deprioritized in favor of the primary cdc.gov URL. Social media results are not usable as evidence sources.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Excellent — all accepted results are norovirus-specific. Location fit: Good for national US level; weak for subnational. Time fit: Partial — December 2024 and early January 2025 are covered; mid-January through February 2025 is not yet evidenced in snippets. The task window ends Feb 28, 2025, so the latter half of the window needs targeted follow-up.
corroboration_potential_assessment: Good for national outbreak counts (multiple sources corroborate the 495 Aug–Dec 11 figure and the Jan 9 weekly counts). Weak for subnational, deaths, hospitalizations, and February 2025 data — these fields need additional targeted queries. The PMC article on GII.17 predominance provides virological context but not case/death counts for the target fields.
